parts.ritual_use: Self-identification + request to Guardians; instructs to avoid Lethe/seek Mnemosyne.

text.english: I am a child of Gē and of starry Ouranos; I thirst and I am perishing; give me to drink from the Lake of Mnemosyne.
text.greek: παῖς γῆς εἰμὶ καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος· διψῶ καὶ ἀπόλλυμαι· τῆς Μνημοσύνης λίμνης πότισόν με.

line_details.english: I am a child of Gē and of starry Ouranos; I thirst and I am perishing; give me to drink from the Lake of Mnemosyne.
line_details.greek: παῖς γῆς εἰμὶ καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος· διψῶ καὶ ἀπόλλυμαι· τῆς Μνημοσύνης λίμνης πότισόν με.
line_details.note: παῖς marks ritual self-identification as offspring of the cosmogonic deities Earth (Gē) and Sky (Ouranos), with ἀστερόεντος “starry” as a fixed epithet. διψῶ καὶ ἀπόλλυμαι expresses the soul’s dire need (“I am thirsty and perishing”). λίμνη “lake/pool” of Mnemosyne (the goddess Memory) contrasts with the Lethe-tradition; some tablets read κρήνη “spring.” πότισόν με is an imperative addressed to the guardians/attendants at the waters, functioning as a password request.

text.english: Do not approach the spring on the left; by the white cypress on the right, seek the Lake of Mnemosyne.
text.greek: ἀριστερὰ πηγὴ—μή πλησιάσῃς· δεξιᾷ παρὰ κυπάρισσον λευκήν· τῆς Μνημοσύνης λίμνην ζήτησον.

line_details.english: Do not approach the spring on the left; by the white cypress on the right, seek the Lake of Mnemosyne.
line_details.greek: ἀριστερὰ πηγὴ—μή πλησιάσῃς· δεξιᾷ παρὰ κυπάρισσον λευκήν· τῆς Μνημοσύνης λίμνην ζήτησον.
line_details.note: The line is deliberately elliptical and directional: δεξιᾷ means “on the right (hand),” and παρὰ with the accusative (“beside”) governs κυπάρισσον λευκήν, “the white cypress,” a set formula in these tablets. The prohibition μή πλησιάσῃς is an aorist-subjunctive negative command. In the Orphic context the left-hand spring is conventionally the water of Lethe (to be avoided), while the initiate is to seek the Lake of Mnemosyne.

text.english: I have come, pure, from the pure; I supplicate the gods.
text.greek: ἥκω καθαρός ἐκ καθαρῶν· ἱκετεύω θεούς.

line_details.english: I have come, pure, from the pure; I supplicate the gods.
line_details.greek: ἥκω καθαρός ἐκ καθαρῶν· ἱκετεύω θεούς.
line_details.note: ἥκω is a present with the sense ‘I have come/am arrived’; καθαρός ἐκ καθαρῶν is a ritual purity formula (‘pure from the pure,’ i.e., from among the pure or through pure rites); καθαρός here is masculine (other tablets show gender variation); ἱκετεύω uses formal suppliant language, likely addressed to chthonic gods in the afterlife context.

text.english: I am a child of Ge and Ouranos; drink from Mnemosyne; shun Lethe.
text.greek: παῖς γῆς καὶ οὐρανοῦ· τῆς Μνημοσύνης ἔκπιε· Λήθην φεῦγε.

line_details.english: I am a child of Ge and Ouranos; drink from Mnemosyne; shun Lethe.
line_details.greek: παῖς γῆς καὶ οὐρανοῦ· τῆς Μνημοσύνης ἔκπιε· Λήθην φεῦγε.
line_details.note: The first phrase is an elliptical self-identification typical of the tablets; “I am” is understood. Ge (Gē) and Ouranos are the deified Earth and Sky; many translate simply “Earth and Sky.” Ἔκπιε is an aorist imperative of ekpinō, “drink out/from,” taking the genitive; in context it means to drink from the spring of Mnemosyne (Memory). Φεῦγε (present imperative) conveys ongoing avoidance—i.e., keep away from Lethe, the river/personification of Forgetfulness. Some recensions read πίε (“drink”) and elsewhere add “starry” to Ouranos (οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος).

text.english: Child of Earth … grant the draught of Mnemosyne.

line_details.english: Child of Earth … grant the draught of Mnemosyne.
line_details.note: The ellipsis marks a lacuna/omission in a well-known Orphic formula that typically reads, “I am a child of Earth and of starry Ouranos …,” followed by the petition at the spring: “grant the draught of Mnemosyne.” γῆ (Earth) here likely evokes the goddess Ge; capitalization signals divinity. πόμα is a ritual ‘draught’ or ‘drink’ (not merely a cup), and δός is an imperative addressed to the underworld guardians of the spring; the implied indirect object is the speaker. Mnemosyne (Memory) is invoked as the contrast to Lethe, whose water must be avoided.

text.english: Say to Persephonē: Bakkhios himself released you.
text.greek: λέγε Περσεφόνῃ· Βάκχιος αὐτὸς ἔλυσέ σε.

line_details.english: Say to Persephonē: Bakkhios himself released you.
line_details.greek: λέγε Περσεφόνῃ· Βάκχιος αὐτὸς ἔλυσέ σε.
line_details.note: Bakkhios = Dionysos. ἔλυσε (“released/loosed”) marks ritual liberation of the initiate. The second-person pronoun σε reflects the tablet’s instructional voice; some witnesses read με (“me”), aligning the reported speech with first person. The sense in either case is that the Bacchic god has freed the initiate.

text.english: I am a child of Earth and of starry Ouranos.
text.greek: παῖς γῆς εἰμὶ καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος.

line_details.english: I am a child of Earth and of starry Ouranos.
line_details.greek: παῖς γῆς εἰμὶ καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος.
line_details.note: παῖς = “child/offspring,” a formulaic self-identification. γῆς and οὐρανός can be read as the primordial deities (Gē/Gaia and Ouranos) or as cosmic Earth and Sky; ἀστερόεντος is the epic epithet “starry.” Transliteration of Ouranos signals the possible theonymic reading in this ritual password.

parts.ritual_use: Password exchange with guardians of the lake.

text.english: The guardians stand by; say: … “I am thirsty; give me to drink from Mnemosyne.”
text.greek: φύλακες παρεστήκασι· εἴπατε... δίψω· πότισόν με ἐκ τῆς Μνημοσύνης.

line_details.english: The guardians stand by; say: … “I am thirsty; give me to drink from Mnemosyne.”
line_details.greek: φύλακες παρεστήκασι· εἴπατε... δίψω· πότισόν με ἐκ τῆς Μνημοσύνης.
line_details.note: φύλακες παρεστήκασι: perfect with present force, “are stationed/stand present,” a stock formula at the spring of Memory. εἴπατε is 2nd plural imperative “say”; many tablets have εἴπε (2nd sg.); the ellipsis signals the standard password (e.g., “I am a child of Earth and starry Sky…”). δίψω “I am thirsty/parched”; πότισόν με “give me to drink.” ἐκ τῆς Μνημοσύνης literally “from Mnemosyne,” i.e., from the spring/lake of Memory implied by the Orphic context. Mnemosyne is retained as a theonym.

text.english: There is a road to the right, beside a white cypress; do not take the left-hand road.
text.greek: δεξιᾷ ὁδός· παρὰ κυπάρισσον λευκήν· ἀριστερὰν μὴ λάβοις.

line_details.english: There is a road to the right, beside a white cypress; do not take the left-hand road.
line_details.greek: δεξιᾷ ὁδός· παρὰ κυπάρισσον λευκήν· ἀριστερὰν μὴ λάβοις.
line_details.note: δεξιᾷ is an adverbial/locative dative (“on/to the right”); παρά with the accusative means “by/beside.” κυπάρισσον (acc. sg. fem.) with λευκήν (acc. sg. fem.) = “white cypress,” a recurrent Orphic landmark. ἀριστερὰν μὴ λάβοις is a prohibition; λάβοις (aorist optative) functions jussively in this epigraphic/poetic register, with ὁδόν (“road”) understood from the first clause.

text.english: Like the other initiates, you shall be blessed.

line_details.english: Like the other initiates, you shall be blessed.
line_details.note: μύσταισιν ('initiates') is dative with ὁμοίως ('in like manner'), giving 'like the other initiates.' μάκαρ ('blessed') functions predicatively with ἔσῃ ('you will be'); a vocative reading ('O blessed one') is possible but the predicative sense suits the assurance of the initiate’s blessed status among peers in the afterlife.
